Identified core components on the whiteboard and transcript: S3 (historical data lake), EMR (PySpark ETL cluster), Neptune (graph database host), SQS (real-time event streaming queue), Elastic Beanstalk (core application engine and rules evaluator), RDS (decision log database), Ticketing System (manual review for high-value users), UI and Users (graph consumers via CrazyWall API), and Neptune ML (graph neural network machine learning subsystem).
2. Validated node service types against the allowed vocabulary list: S3 -> S3, EMR -> EMR, NEPTUNE -> Neptune, SQS -> SQS, ELASTIC BEANSTALK -> BeanStalk, USERS -> UserConsumerWebMobile, UI -> ThirdParty, RDS -> RDS, TICKETING SYSTEM -> ThirdParty, NEPTUNE ML -> Neptune.
3. Segmented workflows into chronological flows: Flow 0 for historical ETL processing into Neptune; Flow 1 for real-time event streaming, graph querying, and decision persistence in RDS; Flow 2 for routing high-value user review tickets via Blocking API; Flow 3 for serving graph data to Users and UI via CrazyWall API; and Flow 4 for advanced Neptune ML integration.

graph.name: Careem CrazyWall Fraud Detection Architecture
graph.categories: Security, Analytics & Data Lakes, Machine Learning
graph.notes: Careem's CrazyWall system combines historical graph ETL on S3/EMR and real-time processing via SQS, Elastic Beanstalk, and Amazon Neptune to detect fraud across services with 90% precision, blocking over 35,000 fraud actors and incorporating Neptune ML for advanced graph deep learning.

nodes.name: S3
nodes.notes: Hosts historical user data in a data warehouse running on Hive.

nodes.name: EMR
nodes.notes: Runs PySpark ETL pipeline to extract, transform, and load historical data into Neptune.

nodes.name: NEPTUNE
nodes.notes: Fully managed graph database holding historical snapshot and real-time network of user identities.

nodes.name: SQS
nodes.notes: Queues real-time application events generated by Pi Event Processor.

nodes.name: ELASTIC BEANSTALK
nodes.notes: Core engine executing transformation, graph querying, and simple rule-based fraud classification (achieving ~90% precision).

nodes.name: USERS
nodes.notes: End users accessing identity and graph context via CrazyWall API.

nodes.name: UI
nodes.notes: Internal UI application allowing teams across Careem to visualize user nodes and edges.

nodes.name: RDS
nodes.notes: Stores fraud classification decisions for all evaluated actions.

nodes.name: TICKETING SYSTEM
nodes.notes: Manual review ticketing queue for high-value customers flagged for potential blocking.

nodes.name: NEPTUNE ML
nodes.notes: Integrated graph convolutional network ML subsystem for automated deep learning fraud predictions.

edges.notes: Historical data extracted from Hive on S3 into EMR cluster.
EMR PySpark ETL loads transformed user identity graph into Neptune.
Real-time app events streamed from SQS into Elastic Beanstalk.
Elastic Beanstalk updates graph database with real-time transformed event.
Elastic Beanstalk queries user identity and graph neighbors for rule evaluation.
Fraud classification decision saved to RDS.
High-value suspicious accounts routed via Blocking API to Ticketing System for manual review.
Exposes graph queries to users via CrazyWall API.
Exposes graph visualization data to UI via CrazyWall API.
Integrates with Neptune ML to execute deep learning model predictions.
